body.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), every \((\theta,M,P_{\mathrm{obs}},W,\mathcal G(W,\ell))\in\mathfrak M_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{Yang}}(\mathbb R)\), and every \(u,v\in V\), the complete image of \(\tau_{\omega}(v\leftarrow u)\) over all minimum-edge DOG representatives is exactly \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) in \(\text{def:effect-image}\), and \(|S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|\leq q+1\). For every \(s\in S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) there is an attaining \(\omega_s\in\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\); if the image is not a singleton, two such minimum completions furnish observationally equivalent countermodels with unequal labeled total effects. The qualifier is relative Zariski generic over each real canonical coefficient variety, equivalently Lebesgue-almost-everywhere in each stratum's free coefficient coordinates, while source-law separability remains a separate assumption; no probability claim is made for rational inputs.
body.justification: The exact set, not a selected representative, is the population object required for honest causal reporting under DOG equivalence.
body.gap: Salehkaleybar et al. project latent-variable LiNGAM ambiguity onto effects, but their admissible transformations omit measured-variable center changes and known measurement labels; Yang et al. give only a four-node robustness example.
body.consumer: A measurement-error analyst can distinguish a robust effect from a finite list of observationally indistinguishable alternatives and receive attaining models for sensitivity analysis.
